subject: physics
question_text: Obtain expressions for the velocity and the acceleration of a particle in simple harmonic motion at a displacement y from the mean position.

verification.note: PREDICTED — Session 89 enumeration sweep (archetype × object grid over the NCERT chapter): this question has not appeared in any paper or source book we hold, but the chapter contains it and the 2-mark/4-mark format admits it. Authored as a lean card; promote to a full card when a paper season or a Telangana IPE teacher validates the cell. Split invented, as everywhere.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The displacement
lines: Take the particle to start from the mean
position. Its displacement after a time t is
where A is the amplitude and ω the angular
steps.why: Starting at the mean position is a choice, not a law; starting at an extreme gives a cosine instead, with the same physics.
common_mistakes: Treating y = A sin ωt as the only possible form rather than one choice of starting instant.

recall.must_convey: That the displacement is y equals A sin omega t.
accept: y equals A sin omega t
reject: v equals omega root A squared minus y squared

steps.memory_tip: sin 0 = 0, so y = A sin ωt starts the particle at the mean position.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Say where the particle starts before writing y = A sin ωt.

steps.label: The velocity

lines.text: v = dy/dt = A ω cos ωt

lines: To write this in terms of y instead of t, use
sin ωt = y/A and cos ωt = √(1 − sin²ωt):

lines.text: v = A ω √(1 − y²/A²) = ω √(A² − y²)

steps.why: The version in y is the useful one — it gives the speed at a stated position without needing to know the time.
common_mistakes: Leaving the answer as A ω cos ωt when the question asks for it at a displacement y.

recall.must_convey: That v is A omega cos omega t, which becomes omega root A squared minus y squared.
accept: omega root A squared minus y squared
reject: y equals A sin omega t
heard_as: root A squared minus y squared

steps.memory_tip: Check the two ends: y = 0 gives ωA, and y = A gives 0. Both are correct.
steps.margin_note: Two marks here. Write v in terms of t first, then convert it to v in terms of y.

steps.label: The acceleration

lines.text: a = dv/dt = −A ω² sin ωt = −ω² y

lines: v is largest at y = 0 and a is largest at y = ±A.
steps.why: a = −ω²y is the definition of SHM recovered from the algebra, which is the check that the whole derivation is consistent.
common_mistakes: Losing the minus sign, which would describe a body pushed away from the centre.

recall.must_convey: That a equals minus omega squared y, and v is largest at the mean position while a is largest at the extremes.
accept: a is minus omega squared y
v largest at the mean position

steps.memory_tip: Both boxed answers must be in y, with no t left anywhere.
steps.margin_note: The last mark. Box the pair together and keep the minus sign on a.

insider_note: The velocity step is two of the four marks, and it must end in y — stopping at A ω cos ωt leaves the question unanswered.
